pins.title: Fix it there
pins.sub: Tape wrapped around your bottle, a length of cord and a small multi-tool fix a lot of trail problems. Ours has a knife, scissors, a screwdriver and a saw. No pliers.

pins.title: Trail repair kit
items: Tape wrapped around your bottle
A few feet of cord
A small multi-tool or knife
Two safety pins for torn fabric
A spare boot lace
pins.sub: Free printable checklist: tap the pin.

pins.title: Cleats on first
pins.sub: Packed snow in the lot often refreezes into ice. Pull the cleats on toe first, then over the heel, before you step out of the car.

pins.title: Keep it warm
pins.sub: Cold slows the battery, so the light dims or shuts off early. Keep it in an inside pocket until dark and carry a spare light. Free guide on the blog: tap the pin.

pins.kicker: Lost your group in the fog?
pins.title: Three blasts
items: Three short blasts: the call for help
A whistle carries further than shouting
It still works when you're hoarse
Clip it outside your pack, in reach
Everyone carries their own

pins.title: Dig a cathole
items: 6 to 8 in (15-20 cm) deep
200 ft (about 70 steps) from water
Away from the trail and camp
Fill it in, cover with leaves
Pack out toilet paper if asked

pins.title: Carry a spare
items: Check your laces before each hike
Measure the old lace for the length
Double-knot them for a long day
Keep a spare pair in your pack
A spare lace is a tie-down too

pins.title: Wear orange
items: A blaze orange hat and vest
Orange on your dog too
Skip white and brown clothing
Talk so hunters hear you
Check your state for the dates
pins.sub: Free guide on the blog: tap the pin.

pins.title: Tioga Road is shut
pins.sub: It usually closes from November until late spring. Yosemite Valley stays open all year: check roads and chain rules on nps.gov. A printable 30-page trip planner.

pins.title: Train this winter
pins.sub: Eight weeks, five short sessions a week, no gym: walks, stairs or a hill and a chair. A printable plan with weekly logs in miles and km.
